prompt: Review this anchor as its assigned subagent. Enumerate ALL requirements, qualifications, edge cases and scenarios. Inspect all supplied implementation and test fragments and trace each aspect to implementation behavior and actual test assertions or justified TODO/N/A evidence. Passing tests and associations alone are insufficient. Follow helpers and capture every additional source dependency with cargo meta review read ANCHOR PATH [selector] before completing the report. Explain prerequisites for justified TODO tests; do not claim deferred behavior is implemented. Distinguish source inspection from commands actually executed. Write a JSON report containing reviewer, report, and requested_edits. Leave requested_edits empty only when every aspect is accounted for and no edits are needed. Otherwise list concrete changes, including missing tests or justified TODO tests with prerequisite comments. Run cargo meta review record ANCHOR REPORT_FILE to finish. After edits or stale-input rejection, run cargo meta review start ANCHOR and review the fresh inputs. The gate fails until a current report with no requested edits is recorded. Dependency capture is agent-declared.
coordinator_instructions: Review only your assigned anchor using the sage-review-checklist skill and its start/read/record workflow. Capture these instructions with start --instructions /tmp/anchor-review-instructions.txt. Use captured source context; do not import old approvals or uncaptured coordinator conclusions. Write only your anchor's validations directory and a unique report file under /tmp. Coordinate production, test, and association edits with the coordinator before making them because concurrent reviewers may capture the same files. Capture essential dependencies using review read; report any necessary association additions for coordinated handling. Existing TODO/N/A evidence must be individually justified and remain deferred; do not claim passing placeholders verify functionality. Distinguish source review from tests actually run. On a suspected behavioral violation, coordinate a regression test and follow the skill rather than rubber-stamping. Return a concise summary of the recorded outcome or precise unresolved finding. Do not commit or change unrelated files.

contents: Before any expectation in one test invocation is compared in updating mode,
the runner completes fixture validation, compilation, annotation validation,
observation collection, independent exhaustive diagnostic matching for both Sage
and rendering of every requested output. All resulting snapshot strings are
prepared before any updating expectation assertion runs. A failure in any of those
steps prevents all snapshot writes for that invocation. After they succeed,
`UPDATE_EXPECT=1` may update observation, diagnostic, and requested query representations.
It never adds source markers, changes compiler conditions, or accepts an
unmatched diagnostic. Other independent Cargo tests may update their own
expectations; this is not a workspace-wide filesystem transaction.
The implementation separates preparation from expectation comparison. Preparation
returns either all validated, rendered results or a failure, without invoking
`expect-test` assertions. The caller stops on failure and compares the returned
results against the supplied expectations only on success. An implementation
comment at that boundary explains why this ordering prevents partial updates
when preparation fails; no separate transaction mechanism is required.

A validation records an agent's assessment of one specification anchor against
its implementation and tests. The saved context lets `cargo meta` check whether
that assessment still applies. Running tests remains a separate obligation.
The main agent discovers review work through a failing `cargo meta check` or
the shared Cargo validation test. Diagnostics identify the affected anchors,
explain why they need review, and direct the agent to the review skill. The
skill delegates one subagent per anchor, supplying its ID and an initial prompt.
The subagent obtains its source context through the review commands, so that
the saved inputs are the same inputs it consumes.

Main->>Reviewer: Follow skill, review anchor using initial prompt

The subagent captures inputs and records its report in the validation directory
created by `start`. Starting a review removes its previous output even when the
source has not changed, so an interrupted review cannot reuse an old approval.
Each additional read is saved before its contents are returned. Recording
checks the captured inputs for freshness and preserves them exactly.
A successful `record` is necessary but does not by itself make the gate pass.
The report must request no edits, its inputs must still be current, and every
other anchor must also satisfy the gate. If edits are requested, the main agent
coordinates them and starts fresh reviews for affected anchors. An accepted
review of justified TODO/N/A evidence leaves that status visible; it does not
claim the deferred behavior is implemented.

Claim, implementation, and annotated test source snapshots are stored in `input.json` as
arrays of source lines. Joining an array with newline characters recovers the
snapshot's text, including internal blank lines, whitespace, and markup.
`Selector::WholeFile` selects all contents of the fragment's source file,
including any trailing newline. It carries no additional selector data.
`Selector::LineRange { start, end }` selects a one-based, inclusive range of
lines within the fragment's source file. Lines are delimited by `\n`; selected
text retains the original line endings, including the last selected line's
ending if present. Zero, reversed, or out-of-bounds ranges are invalid.
The saved line numbers are used again when checking freshness, so shifting
content across those boundaries may conservatively make the fragment stale.
`Selector::Claim { anchor_id }` selects the complete claim identified by its

`Selector::Test { crate_name, target, rust_path }` selects the complete annotated
Rust test function within the fragment's source file, including attributes,

`target` uses the correspondence target identity, including kind and name
qualified function within that target. Identically named functions in different
targets are distinct. The containing file need not be included. The selector
stores no line numbers or byte offsets; inserting unrelated lines before an
unchanged test does not make the fragment stale.

whitespace removed. For `.sage` prose, its enclosing common indentation is

The input records every eligible test associated with that anchor in a

The shared `cargo meta check` fails when any current specification anchor lacks

under {spec}`meta.reviews.decisions`. It loads all validation directories, checks

source. At least one test and implementation entry are required.
A validation for an anchor ID absent from the current specification also fails
the gate, even when every current anchor has a passing validation. Diagnostics

reconcile renamed anchors and start fresh validation. Checking and recording
do not silently delete stale anchor IDs. Invalid record formats, unsupported
schema/policy versions, and incomplete records fail the gate. CI and
workspace Cargo tests use this same gate; checking never creates approvals.
For every anchor requiring re-evaluation, `cargo meta check` and the shared
Cargo validation test must fail until the assigned review subagent successfully
runs `cargo meta review record` for that review. Starting a review, capturing inputs,
reading additional context, or drafting a report cannot satisfy the gate.
An interrupted, abandoned, or failed review remains failing; an older report
cannot stand in for the unfinished review.
Recording is necessary but not sufficient: the recorded report must be complete,
request no edits, and still match current inputs. Recording a report that
requests edits, or changing inputs after recording, leaves the gate failing.
Every required anchor must meet these conditions independently.
CLI and Cargo-test failures identify every anchor requiring re-evaluation and

main agent to invoke `.agents/skills/sage-review-checklist/SKILL.md`; they do not
start reviews or alter saved records themselves.
The repository's `sage-review-checklist` skill instructs the main agent to start
one review subagent for each anchor requiring re-evaluation. Each subagent is
given the anchor ID and an initial prompt directing it to run
`cargo meta review start <anchor>` and evaluate the printed inputs. The main
agent supplies any extra instructions or source context as recorded review
The subagent uses `cargo meta review read` for additional source context and
`cargo meta review record` to save its completed report. Only one subagent owns an
anchor's active directory at a time; reviews for different anchors may run in
parallel. The main agent reconciles requested edits, coordinates changes, and
repeats the start/read/record cycle for affected anchors after edits, then runs
`cargo meta check` again. TODO/N/A evidence is reviewed under the same workflow.
Reviewers trace every requirement to implementation code, checking missing
cases and contradictory behavior. They consider the complete associated test
set and explain which assertions exercise which parts of the claim. They identify a plausible
violation and whether those assertions would detect it.
The scenario, expected outcome, and assertion should be clear from the body of
the test function itself. Parsing, fixture construction, and setup helpers are
reasonable. A call such as `verify_everything()` that hides the meaningful
assertions is insufficient evidence: request a clearer test body instead of
approving it from its name or annotation. Reviewers may read helpers to
understand the test, and capture additional helper fragments through the recorded-read command.
A helper edit outside the supplied files and captured reads does not invalidate a saved review. Running the tests can detect
behavioral changes, but the cached review covers only the snapshotted source.
Add implementation associations to include additional essential source files.
When reviewers suspect a bug, they add an anchor-associated regression test
that exercises the intended behavior and run it against the implementation.
A reproduced behavioral failure yields concrete requested edits, with the test,
command, and observed failure in the report. Do not treat a build or environment
failure as reproduction. If a test cannot reproduce the concern, or a reviewer
cannot work out how to write one, consult the user with the concern and attempts;
leave the affected review unresolved until the concern is resolved. New tests
or associations require starting a fresh review before recording a report.
The generated [anchor pages](../anchor/meta/reviews.html) report implementation entries,
annotated tests, explicit TODO/N/A gaps, and saved implementation/test reviews. These
associations do not themselves establish that a test ran.

inline, dedented Rust source; source-line type observations; exhaustive
ERROR/WARN markers; and `expect-test` snapshots. The first version runs Sage
with the real standard library, checks the whole local crate, and can snapshot
its query work. Rustc execution and narrower demand modes follow separately.
examples cover anonymous source and a multi-file crate. This RFD records why
those choices fit Sage and how to establish their evidence.
The next inference anchors need both focused transaction tests and Rust programs
that exercise those transactions through ordinary checking. Existing
`with_test_crate` callbacks can inspect types, but each test manually finds a
function and walks Typed IR to reach an expression. This obscures the claim's
scenario and makes tests sensitive to incidental tree structure.
The existing oracle harness supports diagnostic source annotations and exact
independent emissions. Its filesystem fixtures and separate discovery runner
serve a different purpose: broad conformance. An inline test should instead
be easy to annotate with `#[sage::test(...)]`, run by name through `cargo test`,
and review as one function containing input and expected output.
Type strings can be large. One combined type expectation keeps them outside the
Rust input while allowing automatic updates when representations deliberately
change. Bare `//# ty` markers avoid managing names for individual observations.
Type output retains filenames but omits line numbers, columns, and ranges,
reducing snapshot churn when unrelated source lines move.
Diagnostics need a different balance: their expected location and count should
be obvious in the source, while one snapshot captures the complete rendered
output. Error slugs add indirection without enough benefit.
### Use ordinary tests and existing expectation tooling
A macro is an authoring convenience around a shared runner, not a replacement
for Cargo's test harness. The function's source remains the review unit.
`expect!` expressions stay at their call sites, where `UPDATE_EXPECT=1` can
update them. The macro's source does not enter every semantic claim snapshot.
The runner itself has independent tests and anchors.
Use `indoc!` explicitly for fixture strings, and `expect-test` for expectations.
This avoids a second dedenting algorithm and a new snapshot dependency when
`expect-test` already serves repository tests. A later tooling change must
preserve the blessing and source-review contracts.
### Exercise real semantic paths with useful defaults
An anonymous snippet is a library crate rooted at `src/lib.rs`, not a source
fragment injected into constructed semantic state. Named paths are relative
to the project and must include that same fixed root; they allow nested modules
and directories without an entry-selection option.
The runner materializes a private Cargo project and invokes production
workspace/compiler facilities with real standard-library metadata. The
checked-in inline source plus deterministic generated configuration defines
the project; temporary files are an execution artifact, not hidden inputs. The
fixture receives ordinary library compilation, with `cfg(test)` disabled and
no enabled Cargo features, independently of its enclosing Cargo test.
The default edition follows the pinned toolchain's latest supported edition.
Tests for historical edition behavior choose it explicitly. Upgrading the
toolchain can therefore intentionally change default semantics; edition
regressions should use pinned edition fixtures.
All local bodies are checked by default. Otherwise adding a type marker could
change which errors become visible, or a broken unselected function could
escape the diagnostic contract. This policy is deliberately separate from
future point-demand tests, which will make their narrower entry point explicit.
Real metadata support must not require successful rustc compilation of the
fixture: negative tests must still reach Sage. This follows the separation
between dependency facts and local semantic work. The `sage-host` crate extracts the shared production setup and trace projection; adding a dependency cycle from
`sage-test-harness` back to its consumers is not an acceptable shortcut.
### Keep annotations local and observations readable
All directives share one target-line rule, including inline diagnostic
comments and stacked annotation lines. Dedenting happens before interpreting
line numbers. Tabs are rejected for consistent fixture formatting; Unicode
visual widths do not matter because no column is selected.
`//# ty` observes every source expression whose span starts on its target
line. Multiple siblings and nested expressions starting on that line are all
included; expressions starting elsewhere are omitted. This avoids repeating
the function-body block and other enclosing expressions for every observation.
A selected expression may extend across later lines. Among selected expressions,
children appear before parents and siblings follow source order. Stable source
identities distinguish equal-span expressions. Meaningful coercions appear as
wrappers after their original expressions, exposing both the completed original
type and the coerced type. Other generated elaboration nodes do not multiply
source observations. Compact, single-line source descriptions omit annotation
comments and normalize whitespace between tokens, preserving literal contents
and escaping them where necessary. This keeps formatting edits from obscuring
These are observations of completed checking, never constraints. Expected
text cannot make inference choose a type, and missing completed results must
not turn into a successful snapshot of an invented placeholder.
### Match structured diagnostics, then snapshot presentation
The renderer is not a reliable source of diagnostic identity or location:
it prints context, secondary labels, notes, and potentially macro locations.
Matching uses the diagnostic's primary span and that span's expansion ancestry.
Label locations cannot make a diagnostic eligible: a marker should identify
where the error is reported, rather than a related declaration or contextual
label. Labels and notes remain visible in the rendered snapshot. Each diagnostic
counts only once. Empty spans match the line containing their position, so
insertion-point diagnostics remain expressible with ordinary line markers.
All compilation stages contribute source diagnostics; repeated reporting of
one diagnostic is deduplicated without collapsing distinct identical-looking
Exhaustive one-to-one assignment expresses both location and count. It also
handles overlapping eligible locations correctly: the runner must not fail
because it greedily assigned a diagnostic with a multi-line primary span or
several macro-ancestry locations to the only marker another diagnostic could use. Notes remain attached presentation, not extra
Compiler conditions use `//# ERROR if SAGE` and `//# ERROR if rustc`, with the
same grammar for WARN. Neither type nor diagnostic markers use slugs. The initial implementation ran only Sage. The rustc-default follow-up runs both
compilers and uses structured rustc output to check lines, severity, and counts,
without requiring rustc text snapshots or type extraction. This extension does not replace exact

### Observe demand as well as results
A correct result can still be produced through an overly broad dependency.
An optional query snapshot makes this work reviewable alongside the source.
The first version observes a cold whole-crate demand, separating project setup
from local semantic demand and freezing observations before rendering.
The Inspector already specifies stable semantic trace projection. Reuse that
contract: preserve meaningful parentage and multiplicity, expose unknown work,
and remove incidental IDs rather than comparing raw Salsa debug output.
Do not sort away meaningful execution order to make a snapshot pass. A future
warm/edit/point-demand extension should build on the same capture boundary.
### Bless output without blessing unexpected errors
Automatic updates are useful for unwieldy type representations and diagnostic
formatting. They must not redefine the program's intended behavior. Before
updating any expectation in a test, the runner validates every marker and
selection and matches all diagnostics. It also finishes query projection and
renders every requested output before any updating assertion runs. A failure
while preparing one output must not leave another expectation already updated.
snapshot update in that invocation, including otherwise valid type snapshots.
This guarantee follows from control flow: preparation returns all validated,
rendered results or fails, and only a successful return reaches expectation
comparison. A comment at the implementation boundary should explain this
ordering. Reviewing that separation can establish the guarantee without a
dedicated test that injects failures into every preparation stage. An annotated no-op test records this implementation-only justification for
review; its passing result is not executable evidence of the guarantee.
This is a validation barrier, not a promise to roll back every file write if an
I/O error occurs, nor a transaction across all Cargo tests. Independent tests
may update independently. Changing a marker is a deliberate assertion change:
agents and people must explain the semantic reason before blessing.

is clarified to include inline checked-in sources materialized as Cargo
projects. The harness crate overview and contributing guidance link the new
proposal. The existing oracle contracts and claim snapshot boundary are
- **Manual Typed IR traversal:** retain for focused structural tests, but avoid
requiring it for ordinary source-line type assertions.
- **Filesystem-only fixtures and a custom runner:** useful for the existing
oracle corpus; less convenient for directly annotated, self-contained tests.
- **Caret or range selection:** permits narrower observations, but requires
horizontal alignment and column rules. Line-based observations include all
expressions starting on the line and make those selectors unnecessary.
- **All expressions intersecting or enclosing the line:** repeats the body block
and other broad ancestors at nearly every marker. Start-line selection keeps
observations local while still showing nested expressions on that line.
- **One smallest enclosing expression:** omits other expressions starting on
the line and requires a choice among equal-span semantic nodes.
- **Type slugs with separate snapshots:** require naming each observation and
maintaining a map; bare markers and one ordered snapshot are sufficient.
- **Error slugs with separate snapshots:** adds naming and matching overhead;
inline severity/count markers plus one output snapshot are clearer.
- **Grepping rendered diagnostic output:** confuses displayed context with
diagnostic locations and complicates future rustc integration.
- **Blessing every observed diagnostic:** silently changes acceptance criteria;
marker intent must remain a prerequisite for representation updates.
- **A new snapshot library:** unnecessary for v1; existing `expect-test` already
provides call-site expectations and the established update workflow.
The production host lives in `sage-host`, with the CLI reexporting its public
modules. Source expressions are enumerated from CST and matched to completed
typed nodes by span and kind; missing or ambiguous correspondence fails an
observation. The snapshot formatter freezes type names and diagnostic source
data before ending query capture, then formats without semantic reads.
Future extensions to provenance, especially macro-generated expressions, must
retain that explicit failure behavior. These are implementation choices constrained by
the linked claims, not permission to omit whole-crate checks or substitute
hand-built semantic answers. If provenance requires changing another Design
contract, propose that change before implementing it.
Generated anchors track implementation and reviewed evidence. The shared host
extraction also updates the owning crate models and refreshes affected reviews.
The original `types:` field becomes `observations:` when adding `//# sym`.
Grouping requested symbol and type facts under one expression makes resolution
visible even when competing definitions have identical types, without repeating
source descriptions or maintaining parallel snapshots. Symbol fields precede
type fields regardless of marker order. The initial symbol selector covers
explicit expression paths; field and method selections remain future work.

Every inline fixture now has a specified rustc comparison, including tests that
request only Sage observations. This prevents a passing Sage snapshot from
silently accepting a fixture that rustc rejects. The same pinned compiler and
sysroot supply metadata and check the fixture, but these are independent tasks;
a metadata provider invocation does not constitute conformance evidence.
opt-ins with a quiet command-line default keep incidental lints out of semantic
fixtures without disabling warning tests. The broad `-A warnings` group suppresses even
source-level specific warning opt-ins, so the adapter individually allows the
pinned compiler's warning-by-default lints instead. Both compilers run before diagnostics
are matched, and both checks gate snapshot updates. Differences require an
explicit compiler-qualified marker and investigation, not automatic blessing.
Implementation order is the rustc adapter and independent marker matching,
focused execution/diagnostic tests, then migration of existing fixtures. Audit
each migration against actual compiler output; preserve language intent and
record Sage limitations rather than altering source merely to hide a mismatch.
